overview: OpenAI expands AI‑driven security collaborations and raises bug bounty payouts.
42AI launches a behavior‑predicting world model funded by a $62.5M seed round.
Legal actions target AI data scraping and paywall bypass by browsers.

top.title: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI
top.summary: OpenAI announced a new security sprint partnering with Cathedral to use its models for testing defenses, quadrupling bug bounty rewards and committing $1 billion in subsidized AI access for frontline defenders.

top.title: Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties
top.summary: OpenAI increased its bug bounty payouts, offering up to $30,000 for critical bugs and up to $172,000 with bonuses, adding quality multipliers and a tiered loyalty program for researchers.

top.title: 42AI comes out of stealth with $62.5M and a world model that can ‘predict human behavior’
top.summary: Israeli startup 42AI emerged from stealth with $62.5 M seed funding, claiming its transformer‑based world model can predict individual trader behavior by modeling psychological tendencies.

top.title: The New York Times sues Brave web browser for AI scraping and bypassing paywalls
top.summary: The New York Times and three other publishers sued Brave for allegedly scraping copyrighted content to feed AI models and enabling users to bypass paywalls without permission.

top.title: The latest AI news we announced in October 2026
top.summary: Google recapped October 2026 releases, including Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon models, Genie 4 simulation tool, and new AI safety features like SynthID Detector.

top.title: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
top.summary: MIT Technology Review reported that only 48% of insights from enterprise analytics agents lead to business improvements, highlighting context gaps and overload as key challenges.
